answer: A Persian wedding is the traditional marriage ceremony of Persian-speaking cultures, primarily Iran, blending pre-Islamic and Islamic customs into one shared occasion. The centerpiece is the sofreh aghd, a ceremonial spread laid before the couple that carries symbolic items such as a mirror, candelabras, sugar cones, and fresh herbs. Family members hold a decorated canopy above the couple while an officiant reads the marriage vows, according to the reference cited below. The formal ceremony is followed by the jashn reception, an evening of music, dancing, and a shared meal with extended family and friends.
